newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey govt to enforce army demands on Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turkey govt to enforce army demands on Islamists.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led government said on Thursday it would rigorously enforce a crackdown on religious activism demanded by the secularist military.
"Our government is committed against the reactionary danger," cabinet spokesman Lutfu Esengun told reporters after ministers debated a list of demands from the generals.
Istanbul stocks closed 4.66 percent up on hopes of government stability.
The military-dominated National Security Council (MGK) told Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition late last month to crack down on Islamist activism.
Esengun, a member of Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party, said politicians and bureaucrats would start work on fulfilling the wishes of the powerful generals.
"The relevant ministries will carry out short-term, medium-term and long-term projects. If orders, new laws or changes to existing laws are needed they will be carried out swiftly," he said.
Erbakan became modern Turkey's first Islamist leader last June. The warning from the secularist armed forces had caused dissent within his coalition with secularist Tansu Ciller's True Path Party.
"The MGK decisions will be carried out to the letter," said Defence Minister Turhan Tayan, a member of Ciller's wing.

Erbakan's Islamists had upset the army in recent months with plans to increase the role of religion in public life. The generals responded with orders for a return to rigid secularism. Their demands include enforcing a ban on Islamic dress and restricting religious education.
